revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Overtime Hours Limit
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen's team can use at most 40 hours of overtime this week to close the case. So far the team has logged 26 hours. Write an inequality for the additional overtime hours t the team can still use, solve it, and graph the solution set on a number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The inequality is 26 + t ≤ 40. Subtracting 26 from both sides: t ≤ 40 − 26 = 14. Since ≤ includes the boundary, graph a closed circle at 14 and shade left (toward smaller values), meaning the team can use 14 or fewer additional overtime hours this week.

questions.stem: A museum has some paintings. After adding 12, they have 45. Which equation models this?
questions.explanation: 'Adding 12' to the original number gives 45: p + 12 = 45. Solve: p = 33.
choiceFeedback: Subtracting says the museum LOST paintings, but 12 were ADDED to what they had. Choose the operation that matches 'after adding 12.'
12p means 12 groups of p, which is multiplication. Re-read what actually happened to the paintings the museum already had.
Dividing would split the paintings into 12 equal groups. The museum did something different with the 12.
hints: The museum STARTS with an unknown number of paintings p, then 12 more are ADDED to reach 45.
'Adding 12' means the model joins p and 12 with a plus sign, and the total 45 goes after the equals sign.
Write the story in order: p, plus 12, equals 45. Which choice matches without switching the operation?
questions.stemEs: Un museo tiene algunas pinturas. Después de agregar 12, tiene 45. ¿Qué ecuación representa esta situación?
questions.explanationEs: «Agregar 12» al número original da 45: p + 12 = 45. Resuelve: p = 33.
hintsEs: El museo EMPIEZA con un número desconocido de cuadros p y luego se AGREGAN 12 más para llegar a 45.
'Agregar 12' significa que el modelo une p y 12 con un signo más, y el total 45 va después del signo igual.
Escribe la historia en orden: p, más 12, es igual a 45. ¿Qué opción coincide sin cambiar la operación?

questions.stem: A detective needs more than 8 hours to finish the investigation. She has already worked 3 hours. Which inequality represents the additional hours h she needs?
questions.explanation: 3 hours plus additional hours h must be more than 8: 3 + h > 8. Solve: h > 5.
choiceFeedback: The equals sign pins her total to EXACTLY 8 hours, but she needs more than 8. Keep the total 3 + h and swap in the comparison the story demands.
This compares the extra hours to 3, but 3 is the time already worked, not the goal. It is the total of both amounts that has to pass 8.
The 8 and the 3 have swapped jobs here. 8 is the total she must go past, and 3 is what she has already finished.
hints: There are two time pieces: the 3 hours already worked and the extra hours h. Together they must pass 8 hours.
'More than 8' means the TOTAL of 3 + h sits on the big side of a strict inequality — not an equals sign.
Combine first: 3 + h. Then compare that total to 8 using the strict 'more than' symbol. Which choice is built that way?
questions.stemEs: Una detective necesita más de 8 horas para terminar la investigación. Ya trabajó 3 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa las horas adicionales h que necesita?
questions.explanationEs: 3 horas más las horas adicionales h deben ser más de 8: 3 + h > 8. Resuelve: h > 5.
hintsEs: Hay dos partes de tiempo: las 3 horas ya trabajadas y las horas extra h. Juntas deben pasar de 8 horas.
'Más de 8' significa que el TOTAL de 3 + h queda del lado grande de una desigualdad estricta, no de un signo igual.
Combina primero: 3 + h. Luego compara ese total con 8 usando el símbolo estricto de 'más de'. ¿Qué opción está armada así?

questions.stem: Which model is correct for: 'A number divided by 6 equals 7'?
questions.explanation: Divided by 6 is n / 6. Equals 7 means = 7. So n / 6 = 7.
choiceFeedback: "Divided" means division, not multiplication.
That shows subtracting 6. The words say divided by 6.
Use division here, not addition.
hints: Spot the operation phrase: 'divided by 6'. That phrase gives you the symbol between n and 6.
Keep the sentence order — the number n comes first, then the division by 6, then 'equals 7'.
Write n / 6 on the left and 7 on the right. Which choice shows division rather than multiplying or adding 6?
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué modelo es correcto para: 'Un número dividido entre 6 es igual a 7'?
questions.explanationEs: Dividido entre 6 es n / 6. Es igual a 7 significa = 7. Entonces n / 6 = 7.
hintsEs: Identifica la frase de operación: 'dividido entre 6'. Esa frase te da el símbolo entre n y 6.
Conserva el orden de la oración: el número n va primero, luego la división entre 6 y luego 'es igual a 7'.
Escribe n / 6 a la izquierda y 7 a la derecha. ¿Qué opción muestra división en vez de multiplicar o sumar 6?

reviewHighlights.rule: Modeling Real-World Scenarios with Equations & Inequalities
steps: 1. Define the variable and units in the scenario
3. Write the algebraic model, solve with inverse operations, and check in context
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving is matching the wrong model to a key phrase. For 'the getaway car held no more than 6 bags,' students often write the equation b = 6 instead of the inequality b ≤ 6, because they see one number and assume it must be exact. The same mistake happens in reverse: for 'the reward split equally among 5 people gave each $40,' students sometimes write the inequality 5p ≥ 40 instead of the equation 5p = 40, because 'split equally' sounds like it could mean a range. Before you submit, ask: does this phrase give one exact value (equation, =) or a limit/range (inequality, <, >, ≤, ≥)?

level1.stem: A bus can carry at most 48 passengers. There are already 31 on board. Which inequality shows how many more can board?
level1.explanation: 'At most 48' means the total must be ≤ 48. So 31 + p ≤ 48. Solve: p ≤ 17.
choiceFeedback: Your total 31 + p is built right — the symbol is the problem. 'At most' is a ceiling: can the bus legally leave exactly full? Pick the symbol that allows it.
An equals sign forces the bus to end up exactly full. Think about whether “at most” also allows a total below the limit.
Subtracting takes away the 31 riders who are already aboard. They belong with the new riders, not apart from them.
hints: The bus already has 31 riders, and p more may board — but the TOTAL cannot pass 48.
'At most 48' allows exactly 48 but nothing above it, so you need the symbol with the 'or equal' bar, not > or =.
Add the parts first: 31 + p. Then cap that sum at 48 with the 'at most' symbol. Which choice matches?
level1.stemEs: Un autobús puede llevar como máximo 48 pasajeros. Ya hay 31 a bordo. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra cuántos más pueden subir?
level1.explanationEs: «Como máximo 48» significa que el total debe ser ≤ 48. Entonces 31 + p ≤ 48. Resuelve: p ≤ 17.
hintsEs: El autobús ya lleva 31 pasajeros y pueden subir p más, pero el TOTAL no puede pasar de 48.
'A lo sumo 48' permite exactamente 48 pero nada por encima, así que necesitas el símbolo con la barra de 'o igual', no > ni =.
Suma primero las partes: 31 + p. Luego limita esa suma a 48 con el símbolo de 'a lo sumo'. ¿Qué opción coincide?

level1.stem: (Lesson 8.4) Which inequality represents: 'The temperature is less than 40 degrees'?
level1.explanation: 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
choiceFeedback: Your symbol opens toward temperatures ABOVE 40. 'Less than 40' lives on the other side — which way should the symbol point?
The ≤ symbol lets the temperature be exactly 40. 'Less than 40' leaves 40 out.
An equals sign pins the temperature to a single value, but this situation describes a whole range of temperatures.
hints: Find the comparison phrase: 'less than 40 degrees'. Does 40 itself count, or only temperatures below it?
'Less than' with no 'or equal to' means a strict symbol — no bar underneath — pointing toward the smaller side.
Test a value: is 35 degrees 'less than 40'? Yes — so pick the strict symbol that puts t on the smaller side of 40.
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'La temperatura es menor que 40 grados'?
level1.explanationEs: 'Menor que' significa <, así que la desigualdad es t < 40.
hintsEs: Halla la frase de comparación: 'menos de 40 grados'. ¿Cuenta el 40 mismo o solo las temperaturas por debajo?
'Menos que' sin 'o igual a' significa un símbolo estricto —sin barra debajo— apuntando hacia el lado menor.
Prueba un valor: ¿35 grados es 'menos de 40'? Sí, así que elige el símbolo estricto que pone t del lado menor de 40.

level1.stem: (Lesson 8.4) Which inequality represents: 'You must be at least 48 inches tall to ride'?
level1.explanation: 'At least' means greater than or equal to, so h ≥ 48.
choiceFeedback: So close — test the boundary. Does a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall get to ride? Your strict symbol turns that rider away.
This describes riders who are too short to ride. Check which direction the symbol opens.
This would let anyone shorter than 48 inches ride. 'At least 48' makes 48 the smallest allowed height, not the largest.
hints: 'At least 48' — ask yourself: can a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall ride? That decides whether 48 is included.
When the boundary value is allowed, you need a symbol with the 'or equal to' bar under it.
Allowed heights are 48, 49, 50, and up. Pick the symbol that includes 48 itself AND points toward bigger numbers.
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Debes medir al menos 48 pulgadas de estatura para subir'?
level1.explanationEs: 'Al menos' significa mayor que o igual a, así que h ≥ 48.
hintsEs: 'Al menos 48': pregúntate si alguien que mide EXACTAMENTE 48 pulgadas puede subir. Eso decide si el 48 se incluye.
Cuando el valor del límite sí se permite, necesitas un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual a' debajo.
Las estaturas permitidas son 48, 49, 50 y más. Elige el símbolo que incluya el 48 Y apunte hacia los números mayores.

level1.explanation: x < 5 means 5 is NOT included (open circle) and values less than 5 are shaded (left).
choiceFeedback: The direction is right, but < does not include 5, so the circle stays open.
This shades the values above 5. Test a number like 7 in x < 5 and see whether it belongs in the solution set.
This both fills in 5 and shades the larger side. Try x = 5 and x = 7 in the inequality — check whether either one makes it true.
hints: Every inequality graph asks two questions: is 5 itself a solution (circle type), and which side holds the solutions (shading)?
Strict symbols like < exclude the boundary, so check whether 5 makes x < 5 true. Then shade toward test values that work.
First step: 5 < 5 is false, so 5 is NOT included — that fixes the circle type. Now test x = 4 to find the shading direction.
level1.explanationEs: x < 5 significa que 5 NO está incluido (círculo abierto) y se sombrean los valores menores que 5 (hacia la izquierda).
choicesEs: Círculo abierto en 5, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo cerrado en 5, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo abierto en 5, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 5, sombreado a la derecha
hintsEs: Toda gráfica de desigualdad hace dos preguntas: ¿es 5 mismo una solución (tipo de círculo) y de qué lado están las soluciones (sombreado)?
Los símbolos estrictos como < excluyen el límite, así que revisa si 5 hace verdadera x < 5. Luego sombrea hacia los valores de prueba que sí funcionan.
Primer paso: 5 < 5 es falso, así que 5 NO se incluye; eso fija el tipo de círculo. Ahora prueba x = 4 para hallar la dirección del sombreado.

level1.explanation: x ≥ 3 means 3 IS included (closed circle) and values greater than or equal to 3 are shaded (right).
choiceFeedback: The direction is right, but ≥ includes 3, so the circle should be filled in.
This shades the numbers below 3. Test x = 1 in x ≥ 3 to see whether small values satisfy the inequality.
This leaves 3 out and shades the smaller side. Check whether x = 3 makes x ≥ 3 true, and test x = 1 as well.
hints: Check the symbol: ≥ has the 'or equal' bar. What does that bar mean for the circle at 3?
The bar means 3 IS a solution, so the circle gets filled in. Then a quick test value tells you the shading side.
First step: 3 ≥ 3 is true, so 3 is included. Now test x = 10 — is 10 ≥ 3 true? Shade toward that side.
level1.explanationEs: x ≥ 3 significa que 3 SÍ está incluido (círculo cerrado) y se sombrean los valores mayores o iguales que 3 (hacia la derecha).
choicesEs: Círculo cerrado en 3, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo abierto en 3, sombreado a la derecha
Círculo cerrado en 3, sombreado a la izquierda
Círculo abierto en 3, sombreado a la izquierda
hintsEs: Revisa el símbolo: ≥ tiene la barra de 'o igual'. ¿Qué significa esa barra para el círculo en el 3?
La barra significa que 3 SÍ es solución, así que el círculo se rellena. Luego un valor de prueba te dice el lado del sombreado.
Primer paso: 3 ≥ 3 es verdadero, así que el 3 se incluye. Ahora prueba x = 10: ¿es 10 ≥ 3 verdadero? Sombrea hacia ese lado.

level2.stem: A student solved 4n = 52 and got n = 13. Is the answer reasonable if n represents the number of notebooks in a box?
choices: Yes — 13 notebooks per box is reasonable
Yes — but only if n is a fraction
level2.explanation: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 notebooks per box is a reasonable whole number answer.
choiceFeedback: Too many by what measure? A box holding 13 notebooks is ordinary. Reasonableness asks whether the number fits the situation, not whether it feels big.
48 comes from subtracting 4 from 52, but 4n means 4 times n. Multiplication is undone with division.
Notebooks are counted in whole numbers, and substituting the solution back into 4n = 52 works out exactly. No fraction is needed here.
hints: 'Reasonable' asks two things: does the math check out, AND does the number make sense for notebooks in a box?
Check the math first: multiply 4 by 13 and see if it rebuilds 52. Then judge whether that count fits a real box of notebooks.
Compute 4 × 13. Does it equal 52? Then ask: could a box realistically hold that many notebooks? Match your reasoning to one choice.
level2.stemEs: Un estudiante resolvió 4n = 52 y obtuvo n = 13. ¿Es razonable la respuesta si n representa el número de cuadernos en una caja?
level2.explanationEs: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 cuadernos por caja es una respuesta razonable con un número entero.
choicesEs: Sí — 13 cuadernos por caja es razonable
Sí — pero solo si n es una fracción
hintsEs: 'Razonable' pregunta dos cosas: ¿cuadran las cuentas Y tiene sentido ese número de cuadernos en una caja?
Revisa primero las cuentas: multiplica 4 por 13 y ve si reconstruye 52. Luego juzga si esa cantidad cabe en una caja real de cuadernos.
Calcula 4 × 13. ¿Da 52? Luego pregunta: ¿podría una caja tener realmente esa cantidad de cuadernos? Une tu razonamiento con una opción.

level2.stem: Room 2: The vault keypad clue reads, 'A number of stolen coins plus 6 equals 14.' Solve x + 6 = 14 to find the code x.
level2.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 14 − 6 = 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 14 − 6 = ___.
6 is a number already given in the equation, not the unknown. Undo the +6 to find what x has to be.
Check this one by substituting it back: your value plus 6 has to land exactly on 14.
level2.stemEs: Sala 2: la pista del teclado de la bóveda dice: 'Un número de monedas robadas más 6 es igual a 14'. Resuelve x + 6 = 14 para hallar el código x.
level2.explanationEs: Resta 6 en los dos lados: x = 14 − 6 = 8. Comprueba: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
hints: An equation is a balance — whatever you do to one side, you do to the other.
The 6 is being added to x, so undo it with the opposite operation, subtraction.
Subtract 6 from both sides so that x stands alone, then work out 14 − 6.
hintsEs: Una ecuación es un equilibrio: lo que le haces a un lado, se lo haces al otro.
Al x se le está sumando 6, así que deshazlo con la operación contraria, la resta.
Resta 6 en los dos lados para que la x quede sola y luego calcula 14 − 6.

level2.stem: Room 3: A sign warns, 'The safe holds at most 20 gold bars.' Which inequality models the number of bars x?
level2.explanation: 'At most 20' means 20 or fewer, so x ≤ 20.
choiceFeedback: That points the wrong way. 'At most 20' means 20 or fewer.
This allows more than 20 bars, but the sign says the safe cannot go past 20. Check which direction “at most” points.
An equals sign says the safe always holds exactly 20. Think about whether fewer bars would break the rule on the sign.
level2.stemEs: Sala 3: un letrero advierte: 'La caja fuerte guarda como máximo 20 barras de oro'. ¿Qué desigualdad representa el número de barras x?
level2.explanationEs: «Como máximo 20» significa 20 o menos, así que x ≤ 20.
hints: Inequality symbols come straight from word clues like “at most”, “no more than”, “at least”, and “more than”.
“At most 20” means the safe can hold 20, or any number below 20, but never more.
Decide first whether the symbol should include 20 itself, then decide which way it points — toward the smaller numbers or the larger ones.
hintsEs: Los símbolos de desigualdad vienen directamente de palabras clave como «como máximo», «no más de», «por lo menos» y «más de».
«Como máximo 20» significa que la caja fuerte puede guardar 20, o cualquier número menor que 20, pero nunca más.
Decide primero si el símbolo debe incluir el 20, y luego decide hacia dónde apunta: hacia los números menores o hacia los mayores.

level2.stem: Room 4: A locked drawer clue reads, 'Five identical evidence boxes weigh 60 pounds in all.' Solve 5w = 60 for each box's weight w.
level2.explanation: Divide both sides by 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 pounds. Check: 5 × 12 = 60 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Divide both sides by 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = ___ pounds.
300 comes from multiplying 5 × 60, but the 60 pounds already includes all five boxes. Multiplication is undone with division.
65 comes from adding 5 and 60, but 5w means 5 times w. Look again at the operation between the 5 and the w.
level2.stemEs: Sala 4: la pista de un cajón cerrado dice: 'Cinco cajas de evidencia idénticas pesan 60 libras en total'. Resuelve 5w = 60 para hallar el peso w de cada caja.
level2.explanationEs: Divide los dos lados entre 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 libras. Comprueba: 5 × 12 = 60 ✓
hints: In 5w, the 5 and the w are multiplied, so undoing it takes the opposite operation.
Divide both sides by 5 so that w is alone on one side.
Set up 60 ÷ 5 to find the weight of a single box, then check by multiplying your answer by 5.
hintsEs: En 5w, el 5 y la w se multiplican, así que deshacerlo requiere la operación contraria.
Divide los dos lados entre 5 para que la w quede sola en un lado.
Plantea 60 ÷ 5 para hallar el peso de una sola caja y después comprueba multiplicando tu respuesta por 5.

level2.prompt: Create two word problems about the same situation: one that requires an equation and one that requires an inequality. Solve both and explain why the models are different.
level2.sentenceFrame: Equation problem: ___. Model: ___. Solution: ___. Inequality problem: ___. Model: ___. Solution: ___. The models are different because ___.
level2.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: Use the same situation twice: one question asks for an EXACT amount, the other sets a limit or a minimum.
Choose clue words on purpose: 'exactly' or 'in total' for your equation; 'at least', 'at most', or 'more than' for your inequality.
Pick a scene, like saving money. Write 'I saved exactly $__' for the equation, then 'I need at least $__' for the inequality. Solve both and compare.
level2.explanation: The two models differ because the two questions ask for different things. An equation fits when the situation names one exact amount, like 'I saved exactly $45', so it has a single solution. An inequality fits when the situation sets a minimum or a ceiling, like 'I need at least $45', so a whole range of values works. Same story, different clue words, different symbol.
level2.explanationEs: Los dos modelos son distintos porque las dos preguntas piden cosas distintas. Una ecuación sirve cuando la situación nombra una cantidad exacta, como 'ahorré exactamente $45', así que tiene una sola solución. Una desigualdad sirve cuando la situación pone un mínimo o un tope, como 'necesito al menos $45', así que funciona todo un rango de valores. La misma historia, distintas palabras clave, distinto símbolo.

Escoge una escena, como ahorrar dinero. Escribe 'Ahorré exactamente $__' para la ecuación y luego 'Necesito al menos $__' para la desigualdad. Resuelve ambas y compara.

choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 14 − 6 = ___.
6 is a number already given in the equation, not the unknown. Undo the +6 to find what x has to be.
Check this one by substituting it back: your value plus 6 has to land exactly on 14.
level3.stemEs: Sala 2: la pista del teclado de la bóveda dice: 'Un número de monedas robadas más 6 es igual a 14'. Resuelve x + 6 = 14 para hallar el código x.
level3.explanationEs: Resta 6 en los dos lados: x = 14 − 6 = 8. Comprueba: 8 + 6 = 14 ✓
hints: An equation is a balance — whatever you do to one side, you do to the other.
The 6 is being added to x, so undo it with the opposite operation, subtraction.
Subtract 6 from both sides so that x stands alone, then work out 14 − 6.
hintsEs: Una ecuación es un equilibrio: lo que le haces a un lado, se lo haces al otro.
Al x se le está sumando 6, así que deshazlo con la operación contraria, la resta.
Resta 6 en los dos lados para que la x quede sola y luego calcula 14 − 6.

level3.stem: Room 3: A sign warns, 'The safe holds at most 20 gold bars.' Which inequality models the number of bars x?
level3.explanation: 'At most 20' means 20 or fewer, so x ≤ 20.
choiceFeedback: That points the wrong way. 'At most 20' means 20 or fewer.
This allows more than 20 bars, but the sign says the safe cannot go past 20. Check which direction “at most” points.
An equals sign says the safe always holds exactly 20. Think about whether fewer bars would break the rule on the sign.
level3.stemEs: Sala 3: un letrero advierte: 'La caja fuerte guarda como máximo 20 barras de oro'. ¿Qué desigualdad representa el número de barras x?
level3.explanationEs: «Como máximo 20» significa 20 o menos, así que x ≤ 20.
hints: Inequality symbols come straight from word clues like “at most”, “no more than”, “at least”, and “more than”.
“At most 20” means the safe can hold 20, or any number below 20, but never more.
Decide first whether the symbol should include 20 itself, then decide which way it points — toward the smaller numbers or the larger ones.
hintsEs: Los símbolos de desigualdad vienen directamente de palabras clave como «como máximo», «no más de», «por lo menos» y «más de».
«Como máximo 20» significa que la caja fuerte puede guardar 20, o cualquier número menor que 20, pero nunca más.
Decide primero si el símbolo debe incluir el 20, y luego decide hacia dónde apunta: hacia los números menores o hacia los mayores.

level3.stem: Room 4: A locked drawer clue reads, 'Five identical evidence boxes weigh 60 pounds in all.' Solve 5w = 60 for each box's weight w.
level3.explanation: Divide both sides by 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 pounds. Check: 5 × 12 = 60 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Divide both sides by 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = ___ pounds.
300 comes from multiplying 5 × 60, but the 60 pounds already includes all five boxes. Multiplication is undone with division.
65 comes from adding 5 and 60, but 5w means 5 times w. Look again at the operation between the 5 and the w.
level3.stemEs: Sala 4: la pista de un cajón cerrado dice: 'Cinco cajas de evidencia idénticas pesan 60 libras en total'. Resuelve 5w = 60 para hallar el peso w de cada caja.
level3.explanationEs: Divide los dos lados entre 5: w = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 libras. Comprueba: 5 × 12 = 60 ✓
hints: In 5w, the 5 and the w are multiplied, so undoing it takes the opposite operation.
Divide both sides by 5 so that w is alone on one side.
Set up 60 ÷ 5 to find the weight of a single box, then check by multiplying your answer by 5.
hintsEs: En 5w, el 5 y la w se multiplican, así que deshacerlo requiere la operación contraria.
Divide los dos lados entre 5 para que la w quede sola en un lado.
Plantea 60 ÷ 5 para hallar el peso de una sola caja y después comprueba multiplicando tu respuesta por 5.
